column1: Assessment incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC raised the federal funds rate to 0.75–1.00 percent and will begin balance-sheet runoff on June 1 to address elevated inflation amid Ukraine-related energy shocks and renewed China lockdowns. The April 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates credit supply to businesses remained supportive: domestic banks on net eased standards for C&I loans and multifamily CRE, reduced costs on credit lines, and reported stronger demand tied to inventories, accounts receivable, equipment, and plant investment; construction and nonfarm nonresidential CRE standards were largely unchanged. On the household side, banks eased standards for credit cards and saw stronger demand for HELOCs and auto loans, but reported weaker demand for residential real estate mortgages—consistent with rising rates cooling housing. Foreign banks tightened C&I standards somewhat, a modest offset. Taken together, SLOOS suggests bank intermediation is not yet a binding constraint and should cushion the drag from tighter monetary policy, even as housing and other rate-sensitive activity soften. Net: inflation risks remain elevated and growth headwinds persist, but supportive bank credit conditions tilt the outlook slightly less negative than a purely FSR-based read. sentiment score = -0.10
